swarm.problem: Why does trapped chaos live exponentially longer as a face grows, and what sets the rate?

probability.label: Probability: dice instead of chaos
probability.line: Swap the chaos beneath an edge for coin flips and prove the long lifetime there.
probability.state: Round 2 and an interim note written; only round 1 refereed; lab requests R5-R9 not run.
results: Each edge cell's next state is an independent coin with an explicit bias table.
With both extreme drives possible no state is immortal; lifetime at most exponential.
The sharpest one-step monotone process below the dice model, written exactly.
If both cells beneath agree by a fair coin, lifetime grows exponentially with length.
For independent cells beneath, any one-step monotone comparison dies fast; it cannot prove the law.
Comparisons over several generations must seed nearly at full speed.
Theorem A': any bulk will do
The lower bound needs only that 'none' and 'both' alive beneath stay possible.
A one-step inequality at every living state bounds lifetime from below.
Exact inequality between a ring and a walled interval; the useful half needs an unproved hypothesis.
For the percolation stand-in, lifetime costs at most about 0.48 per cell.
A checkable criterion for exponential lifetime; no certificate found.
Guess: walls, mirrors, ring share one exponent; exact data agree except the ring.
probability.top: Exact tables it asked for ('the result of the round'): coin flips reproduce the 2D rule's symmetry ratios.
probability.next: Use lab R6, R7 to prove 'walls = ring' for dice or write a front version; then the gump face; then a contour certificate.

counting.label: Counting: the map with a trapdoor
counting.line: Count exactly how many starting states have emptied the edge by a given age.
counting.state: Round 2 written; critic's reply interim; lab scripts drafted, never run.
results: Bounds on how soon a measure-preserving map falls into a trapdoor.
A reversible relative of gump keeps its faces alive forever: no route there.
From random soup, chance the 2D edge is empty at age k falls exactly exponentially in length.
Per-cell rates at ages 1 and 2: 0.551535 and 0.467693.
Walls and mirrors at fixed age
At fixed age walls cost at least a ring, a mirror at least half.
Cells beneath a gump face split into cubes; one-step death decided cube by cube.
A lone live cube keeps a slab face alive for k generations.
A long empty stretch keeps its middle empty for a while.
Early rate depends on the soup
The early-age rate depends on starting density, so it is not the long-run exponent.
Up to a fixed age the true rule equals a dice model with enough rows.
A live edge cell makes the cells beneath slightly less likely alive.
Last cell, last triangle over dice
Exact one-step death chances of a lone cell and lone triangle on a gump face.
No finite still pattern holds against an arbitrary outside.
Guess: the limit of early rates is at most the true exponent; untested.
Guess: the limiting early rate stays above zero.
counting.top: Early death is exactly exponential in length, but that early rate is not the long-run one.
counting.next: If early rates level at the steady rate, state C1' as a formula and test c3; if not, drop it and count small gump-face deaths over dice.

path.label: Path: cheapest road to empty
path.line: Find the least unlikely route to an empty face and why its cost scales with area.
path.state: Round 3 interim written; rounds 1-2 refereed; round 3 review and a promised pointer owed.
results: A dead patch refills only from its edge, one cell per generation at most.
A one-step inequality for any face statistic bounds the death rate, no memory assumed.
Deaths = entries into a low set times a committor of the pooled one-step table.
Every permanent loss kills a smallest sealed set: a face in a hull, a band in a wide slab.
Sealed sets are complements of bootstrap-closed sets; their top layer is rigid.
In biased voter dynamics a droplet's death chance is exactly exponential in size.
Four sibling rules share gump's sealed-set facts yet die fast.
Before death a face shrinks; the collapse lengthens with face size.
Hypothesis giving the area law; false as first stated, weaker form untested.
Th: gamma as integral of roots
Guess: gamma is an integral of local one-step roots; a rough estimate gives about 0.21.
A: face is smallest sealed set
Guess for all hulls; exact up to radius 10.
Guess: all 2D geometries share one exponent; rings carry an extra power of length.
Sketched model: walls no power, rings a power; rings disagree at reachable sizes.
path.top: Death rate read from one-step statistics, no memory assumed; for gump a genuine reduction, not circular.
path.next: Sum local roots over the committed tables against lifetimes; exact dice test of the death-age profile; ask the library for contour corrections.

source.label: Source: where randomness comes from
source.line: Use deterministic systems that provably act like dice, and ask what gump's bulk would need.
source.state: Round 3 interim written, unreviewed; the line judges it 'has given what it can'.
results: A suitable deterministic bulk feeds the top layers perfectly fair coins, even with feedback.
Any random automaton with rational odds is the top of a deterministic one.
A confined system cannot supply exact dice for an exponentially long life.
A face's death law depends on the bulk only via the same-time law beneath.
Uncapped, every cell ends up repeating with period at most 2.
A bulk without overcrowding makes no lasting randomness.
Information from beneath passes only at the birth threshold or the cap.
If the drive is never too predictable, lifetime is at most exponential in area.
Exact formula for a lone face cell dying over random cells.
Gump's one-cell row matches dice at density 0.52, in a poorer layer.
A deterministic edge-plus-conveyor automaton: memoryless wait, lifetime exponential in length.
If the drive keeps cells alive often enough, the dice lower bound transfers.
Six live face neighbours kill a cell whatever is beneath; 2D edges cannot.
Guess: deep enough, the exponent ignores the bulk; no exact support.
Class K with a lower bound
A class of drive laws containing gump's with a proved lower bound.
Sketched: a periodic source gives immortality unless its period is huge.
source.top: With probability: a deterministic automaton whose edge provably lives exponentially long, modulo two cited facts.
source.next: Read the round-3 reply; if probability gets T1, state a several-generation Theorem L; else declare 'source: finished'.

alive: Three lines meet here; dice support it, ring unsettled.
Face in a hull, band in a wide slab; needs hypothesis H'.
Rough estimate about 0.21; real sum not done.
swarm.formula: None. Path's guess Th gives about 0.21 'from eight numbers and a ruler', near gump's 0.21-0.22; nothing for 2D's 0.36-0.42.
swarm.theorems: Exponential lifetime is proved only for dice or deterministic relatives near the 'equal cells by a fair coin' anchor, modulo F1, F2; no lower bound for gump or the 2D rule.
